rulings.challenge_claim: Two items on one row. First: the rejected-alternative sentence names a neighbouring unit by its position rather than by verse, a register violation, while the seam itself is otherwise byte-warranted. Second: the front-seam warrant is contradicted by the bytes the row itself quotes -- third-person description already runs in the immediately preceding verse and the row's opening word is a consecutive form binding it to that clause -- and the parashah seg called the opening mark sits at the wrong seam.
rulings.grounds: The two items are DISTINCT defects, not one, and they do not stand at the same strength. (a) The register item stands exactly as filed and needs no reframing: strongest_rejected_alternative reads 'kept together as the row before this one', a cross-unit reference by position where the standing rule requires verse anchoring. (b) The mark-position item stands exactly as filed, and the keying convention it rests on is provable from the inventory itself: a seg is recorded against the verse it FOLLOWS. At the book's eleven parent-frame seams the frame-final verse carries a seg 11 times out of 11 (oshb:Jer.1.3, oshb:Jer.6.30, oshb:Jer.10.25, oshb:Jer.17.27, oshb:Jer.20.18, oshb:Jer.24.10, oshb:Jer.29.32, oshb:Jer.33.26, oshb:Jer.39.18, oshb:Jer.45.5, oshb:Jer.51.64) and the frame-initial verse 0 times out of 11 (parashah tier-3, single-witness). Under that keying the SAMEKH at oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3 falls after the span's FIRST verse -- inside the row -- while the front seam itself carries no seg (inventory: 0 segs at oshb:Jer.9.1 = web:Jer.9.2; absence is never counterevidence). The closing SAMEKH at oshb:Jer.9.5 = web:Jer.9.6 does stand at the back seam. Both span segs are SAMEKH; no PE is in play here. device_notes' claim that setumot open and close the row is therefore half wrong, and the same key is carried in boundary_evidence_refs as front-seam corroboration. (c) The seam-warrant item is REFINED rather than upheld as framed. Both byte facts are true: oshb:Jer.9.1 = web:Jer.9.2 closes in third-person plural description, כִּ֤י כֻלָּם֙ מְנָ֣אֲפִ֔ים עֲצֶ֖רֶת בֹּגְדִֽים (byte tier), and the row's own opening word וַֽיַּדְרְכ֤וּ at oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3 (byte tier) carries the pointed vav plus patah with a doubled following consonant, the consecutive prefix pattern. But the third-person material before the seam sits inside that verse's subordinate causal clause serving the first-person wish, whereas oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3 opens a fresh MAIN clause in third-person description. The warrant is therefore under-specified, not contradicted; what is genuinely absent is the disclosure, since a byte-true consecutive form straddling the row's own front seam argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed, and no field discloses it. (d) NEW, raised by neither item: the row's prose carries bare in-zone coordinates -- the seam 'could instead sit at 9.2 rather than 9.3', and 'a fresh koh-amar onset at 9.7'. Inside the offset zone a bare coordinate resolves to two different verses: read on the web side, 9.7 is the koh-amar onset (web:Jer.9.7 = oshb:Jer.9.6); read on the MT side it is the arrow verse carrying the zone's single ketiv/qere note (oshb:Jer.9.7 = web:Jer.9.8) and no koh-amar at all. The zone-disclosure arm is machine-enforced only on witness-prefixed refs, so prose coordinates of this shape pass unseen; the class recurs at P03-010, P03-011 and P03-013.
rulings.remedy: (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 'kept together as the row before this one' with a verse-anchored formulation naming the two wish-cries at web:Jer.9.1 = oshb:Jer.8.23 and web:Jer.9.2 = oshb:Jer.9.1; no positional cross-unit reference may survive in any field. (2) device_notes AND boundary_evidence_refs: stop presenting oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3 as this row's OPENING mark -- under the inventory's follow-the-verse keying that seg stands inside the span; say instead that the front seam carries no seg (absence is never counterevidence) and keep oshb:Jer.9.5 = web:Jer.9.6 as closing-seam corroboration, both SAMEKH, single-witness, tier-3. (3) boundary_rationale: scope the third-person warrant to the fresh main clause, and disclose the straddling consecutive form at the front seam with its tier. The span is NOT to be moved by this remedy: any respan (e.g. opening after the seg and the neum-YHWH tag at oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3) is a proposal for boss adoption, never author work. (4) Add an explicit dual or numeric qualifier to every bare in-zone coordinate in this row's prose. TESTS the cure must pass: no positional or administrative cross-unit reference anywhere in the row; every parashah citation states which seam it stands at under the follow-the-verse keying; the front-seam warrant survives a full re-read of oshb:Jer.9.1 = web:Jer.9.2 including its causal clause -- the read that killed the original; and no bare chapter.verse coordinate touching web ch 9 or MT 8:23 / MT ch 9 remains without a dual or numeric qualifier.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both edges of the seam warrant lean on translation poetry-line layout, which is not evidence from either witness, while the Hebrew that would actually carry the prose-register claim is left unquoted.
rulings.grounds: The layout digits are right and the objection to relying on them is right in principle: the translation carries 0 poetry lines across web:Jer.9.12 = oshb:Jer.9.11 through web:Jer.9.16 = oshb:Jer.9.15, against 3 at web:Jer.9.11 = oshb:Jer.9.10 and 2 at web:Jer.9.17 = oshb:Jer.9.16; poetry-line breaks are tier-4 translation formatting, never evidence in either direction, and the staged MT extract carries no layout layer, so nothing on the witness side underwrites a register contrast. But 'both edges lean on' it overstates the defect. The opening edge names a byte-spliced unformulaic interrogative onset, מִֽי הָאִ֤ישׁ הֶֽחָכָם֙ (oshb:Jer.9.11 = web:Jer.9.12, byte tier) -- a discourse-frame onset, tier-1. The closing edge names, in the same sentence as the layout remark, the next verse's own title-stack formula with a plural imperative, כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִתְבּֽוֹנְנ֛וּ (oshb:Jer.9.16 = web:Jer.9.17, byte tier) -- tier-1 and wholly independent of layout. Both edges therefore already stand on witness signals; the layout is an impermissible CO-citation, not the load-bearing driver, and the boundary is not in question. The sharper locus, named by neither item, is a different field: observed_substrate_signals records narrative_frame.prose_interlude_in_poetic_context, which files a translation-layout fact into the substrate-signal register where tier-4 formatting can never sit; device_notes then repeats the same fact a third time.
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: delete the two layout clauses ('set in prose where the oracles on either side run in poetry'; 'returns to poetry'), retaining the opening interrogative onset at oshb:Jer.9.11 = web:Jer.9.12 and, at the close, the koh-amar-plus-imperative onset at oshb:Jer.9.16 = web:Jer.9.17, each with its splice and tier named. (2) observed_substrate_signals: drop narrative_frame.prose_interlude_in_poetic_context. oss is a dependent field of the driver set, so re-check the remaining keys, unit_type, confidence and strongest_rejected_alternative after the edit. (3) device_notes: drop the poetry-line sentence, or restate it explicitly as translation formatting carrying no evidential weight in either direction. (4) Add the zone qualifier to the bare coordinates 9.16 and 9.17 in the prose. TEST the cure must pass: delete every layout sentence and the row's two edge warrants must still stand, each naming a byte-spliced witness signal with its tier -- the deletion that killed the original; and no field, prose or oss, may rest a boundary claim on poetry lines, paragraph breaks or verse numbering.

rulings.challenge_claim: The addressee analysis is byte-wrong at the row's opening, the summons imperatives being plural forms addressed to the summoners rather than to the mourning women; the transliteration erases the feminine-plural morpheme that actually marks the turn to the women; and the closing splice runs past its gloss.
rulings.grounds: The opening component is REFUTED on the row's own words. boundary_rationale glosses הִתְבּֽוֹנְנ֛וּ וְקִרְא֥וּ לַמְקוֹנְנ֖וֹת (oshb:Jer.9.16 = web:Jer.9.17, byte tier) as 'consider, and call for the mourning women', treating the mourning-women noun as the OBJECT of the two plural imperatives -- which is exactly what the bytes carry. The row does not address the women at its opening and does not say it does. The defect the item is reaching for is real but sits one field away, in strongest_rejected_alternative, which speaks of 'the women of 9.17-21'. The women are spoken OF in the third person at oshb:Jer.9.17 = web:Jer.9.18, וּתְמַהֵ֕רְנָה (byte tier), with the benefit accruing to a first-person plural group, and oshb:Jer.9.18 = web:Jer.9.19 is a quoted cry from Zion; the address to the women themselves begins only at oshb:Jer.9.19 = web:Jer.9.20 with the feminine-plural imperative שְׁמַ֤עְנָה (byte tier). The rejected alternative therefore assigns three verses to an addressee the bytes withhold, and it contradicts the row's own rationale, which locates the turn correctly. The transliteration defect is real as filed: that same form is rendered 'shim'ah', dropping the ending that carries the feminine-plural addressee the argument depends on -- a byte-checkable form claim held to the same discipline as a digit. The gloss-extent defect is real as filed: the closing splice runs one preposition past its gloss and stops inside a construct chain, where the bytes read כְּדֹ֖מֶן עַל פְּנֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה (oshb:Jer.9.21 = web:Jer.9.22, byte tier). Verified and left standing: the variant-formula disclosure is exact -- the bare-imperative-plus-neum consonantal run stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier), oshb:Jer.9.21 = web:Jer.9.22, against 152 verses for the koh-amar-YHWH shape (sweep: 152 verses, skeleton tier); and all three parashah citations are correctly positioned under the follow-the-verse keying (PE after oshb:Jer.9.15 = web:Jer.9.16 at the front seam, SAMEKH after oshb:Jer.9.18 = web:Jer.9.19 inside, SAMEKH after oshb:Jer.9.21 = web:Jer.9.22 at the close; tier-3, single-witness).
rulings.remedy: (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut the addressee description to the bytes -- the women are addressed from web:Jer.9.20 = oshb:Jer.9.19, not from web:Jer.9.17 = oshb:Jer.9.16 -- or drop the addressee contrast and rest the alternative on the continuity of the death image alone; the field must not contradict boundary_rationale. (2) boundary_rationale: re-transliterate the feminine-plural imperative at oshb:Jer.9.19 = web:Jer.9.20 with its full ending. (3) boundary_rationale: re-cut the closing pair so gloss extent equals splice extent -- either extend the splice through the whole prepositional phrase at oshb:Jer.9.21 = web:Jer.9.22 and gloss it whole, or shorten the splice to the dung noun. (4) Add the zone qualifier to the bare coordinates 9.17-21, 9.21, 9.22 and 9.23 in the prose. TESTS the cure must pass: every transliteration reproduces the ending of the form it names; no splice extends past its gloss or terminates inside a construct chain; and the addressee claim in EVERY field survives a re-read of oshb:Jer.9.16-Jer.9.19 = web:Jer.9.17-Jer.9.20 -- the read that killed the original.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two items on one row. First: boundary_rationale names the production plan's own segmentation of the book alongside the unit's own edge, a register violation, though the formula-driven boundaries and the nations-list disclosure are otherwise sound. Second: the cross-reference propping the opening warrant is an untiered recurrence claim carrying no sweep digit, and the two sites are not the same shape in the bytes, differing precisely in the verse-initial property the warrant rests on.
rulings.grounds: Both items stand, and they are DISTINCT defects in two different sentences of the same field. (a) Register: boundary_rationale closes 'The row and the part both end at 9.26' -- an administrative division of the book, barred from row prose in every field. The sentence carries no textual content, so removing it costs the warrant nothing. (b) Recurrence: the row's opener הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים at oshb:Jer.9.24 = web:Jer.9.25 (byte tier) is verse-initial. The site called the same shape reads לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּֽה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ at oshb:Jer.7.32 = web:Jer.7.32 (byte tier): there the formula is prefixed by the therefore-particle and is NOT verse-initial, so the two sites differ in the one property the onset warrant leans on; the Hebrew is quoted at only one of them; and the claim carries neither a tier label nor a digit. The consonantal run stands in 15 verses book-wide (sweep: 15 verses, skeleton tier), 14 of them with the neum-YHWH tag attached (sweep: 14 verses, skeleton tier) -- a dense formula rather than a distinguishing onset marker, which the row does not say. The boundary itself is untouched by either item and holds independently: the preceding verse closes on its own neum-YHWH tag at oshb:Jer.9.23 = web:Jer.9.24 with a seg following it (parashah tier-3, single-witness) -- the closure-then-fresh-onset configuration the ruled granularity licenses -- and the roster and its verdict at oshb:Jer.9.25 = web:Jer.9.26 are one grammatical sentence. The same bare in-zone coordinate class flagged elsewhere in this cluster is live here too, in the very sentence at (a).
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: delete the closing sentence naming the row and the part; nothing textual is lost, and the bare in-zone coordinate goes with it. (2) boundary_rationale: re-cut the cross-reference -- either splice oshb:Jer.7.32 = web:Jer.7.32 alongside the opener and state the difference (therefore-particle prefix; not verse-initial) with the tier at which the two DO match, or drop the cross-reference and rest the onset on the verse-initial formula plus the neum-YHWH closure at oshb:Jer.9.23 = web:Jer.9.24. Any retained recurrence sentence carries a tier label and an adjacent digit naming the swept object and unit (the consonantal run: 15 verses). (3) If any in-zone coordinate survives anywhere in the prose, give it a dual or numeric qualifier. TESTS the cure must pass: the recurrence claim survives a side-by-side byte read of BOTH sites including the verse-initial property -- the read that killed the original; every recurrence or count sentence carries a tier and a digit-bearing sweep naming its object and unit; and a register sweep finds no administrative, positional or file-order reference in any field.

rulings.challenge_claim: The no-internal-seam warrant is falsified by the bytes the row itself quotes, a sustained singular address to Yahweh interrupting the plural addressees; the same warrant assigns the whole span to one speaker's mouth that the bytes contradict; and the Aramaic island's opening verb is mislabelled an imperative.
rulings.grounds: The item stands. Form class: כִּדְנָה֙ תֵּאמְר֣וּן at oshb:Jer.10.11 = web:Jer.10.11 (byte tier, Aramaic) carries the tav prefix and the paragogic nun of a prefix-conjugation form, and the translation renders it as a modal future, “You shall say this to them” (web:Jer.10.11); no morphology layer is staged, so the label stands or falls on the pointed bytes plus the two renderings, and neither supports 'citation imperative'. That label is also the sharper locus of the contradiction the item names, since the same rationale asserts that no additional discourse imperative interrupts the span while calling this form one: correcting the form class cures both at a single edit. Frame ownership: the row places the mockery in one mouth on the strength of the onset formula at oshb:Jer.10.2 (byte tier), but the span carries at least two further speaker positions the bytes will not put in that mouth -- second-person praise addressed TO Yahweh at oshb:Jer.10.6, גָּד֥וֹל אַתָּ֛ה וְגָד֥וֹל שִׁמְךָ֖ (byte tier), continued at oshb:Jer.10.7, and third-person predication ABOUT Yahweh at oshb:Jer.10.10, וַֽיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ אֱמֶ֔ת (byte tier). A koh-amar claim that does not name which mouth carries which stretch is the one claim this book's formula census will not support. One qualification on the addressee half: the rationale DOES disclose the praise turn before denying an 'additional' one, so this is a self-contradictory criterion rather than a suppressed fact -- still a defect, and the return to the plural addressees at oshb:Jer.10.11 is a further undisclosed turn. The holding is not disturbed: a thematic register alternation is not a tier-1 seam, the default for frame-plus-speech is the larger unit, and the island disclosure is present and correct (inventory: 15 Aramaic-coded morphs, all in that one verse). NEW, raised by neither lens: observed_substrate_signals files the hear-the-word plural imperative of oshb:Jer.10.1 (byte tier) under a word-event key, although the word-event system is a closed set of three shapes that are never blended and a discourse-frame imperative is not one of them; across the book's candidate rows the discourse-imperative signal element appears in 31 oss entries, 28 of them under narrative_frame or speech_formula keys and 3 under a word-event key. Second new item: device_notes places the seg at oshb:Jer.10.11 'inside the span', where under the follow-the-verse keying it stands at the span's CLOSING seam.
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: re-label the Aramaic opener at oshb:Jer.10.11 = web:Jer.10.11 as a prefix-conjugation (modal) form, not an imperative, and re-read the criterion sentence so it no longer denies a signal the same sentence names. (2) boundary_rationale: name the mouth per stretch -- the formula-owned mockery, the second-person praise at oshb:Jer.10.6-Jer.10.7, the third-person predication at oshb:Jer.10.10, and the return to the plural addressees at oshb:Jer.10.11 -- or restate the warrant to claim only that no fresh divine-speech formula, addressee-naming imperative or discourse frame opens a rival unit inside the span. No respan is ordered: the span stands. (3) observed_substrate_signals: re-file the oshb:Jer.10.1 discourse imperative out of the word_event family into the key family the corpus uses for that class, and carry the same order as its own sweep to every row whose oss carries word_event.discourse_imperative_onset (P04-001, P04-003, P04-008). oss is a dependent field, so re-check confidence and strongest_rejected_alternative after the edit. (4) device_notes: state the oshb:Jer.10.11 seg as standing at the closing seam, not inside the span. TESTS the cure must pass: every form-class label in the row is readable off the pointed bytes plus both renderings -- the read that killed the original; no sentence denies a signal the same row names; every koh-amar claim names whose mouth carries which verses; and the oss key set contains no word-event key that is not one of the three attested word-event shapes.

rulings.challenge_claim: The twin cross-reference is an untiered recurrence claim that the consonantal evidence bears only in part, and the ketiv/qere note is argued from an English rendering that cannot register the variant.
rulings.grounds: Both halves check out on the bytes. The narrow claim is exact: יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ closes oshb:Jer.10.16 and the identical run closes oshb:Jer.51.19 (byte tier, both). The wider designation is not: of the five verse pairs, two are byte-identical (oshb:Jer.10.12 against oshb:Jer.51.15; oshb:Jer.10.15 against oshb:Jer.51.18) and three diverge already at skeleton tier -- oshb:Jer.10.13 carries the ketiv/qere doublet where oshb:Jer.51.16 has a single article-less noun, besides two divergent verb forms; oshb:Jer.10.14 carries the refiner noun plene against the defective spelling at oshb:Jer.51.17; and oshb:Jer.10.16 has the defective Jacob noun with an Israel noun before the tribe noun against the plene Jacob and no Israel noun at oshb:Jer.51.19. No tier is named anywhere on the recurrence claim, where campaign practice requires one on every recurrence sentence, so which of these the row asserts cannot be read off it. The ketiv/qere inference is falsified by the witnesses themselves. The note is inventory-true and both forms stand in the source bytes, מִקְצֵ֣ה ארץ הָאָ֑רֶץ at oshb:Jer.10.13. But the parallel verse carries the article-less מִקְצֵה אָ֑רֶץ at oshb:Jer.51.16 (byte tier), and the translation renders the two identically -- “from the ends of the earth” (web:Jer.10.13) and “from the ends of the earth” (web:Jer.51.16) -- so the English cannot register the article and is evidence for neither reading. A witness-internal variant is never adjudicated from a translation. The row's edges are unaffected: the participial opening is verse-initial at oshb:Jer.10.12 and the name-formula verse-final at oshb:Jer.10.16 (byte tier, both), and the seg keyed after oshb:Jer.10.11 stands at the front seam exactly as the row says (parashah tier-3, single-witness).
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale and device_notes: tier-label the recurrence and scope it -- the closing name-formula is byte-identical at oshb:Jer.10.16 and oshb:Jer.51.19; if the wider pairing is kept as texture, state the tier at which it holds and that three of the five verse pairs diverge in the consonants. (2) device_notes: delete the inference that the qere supplies the definite reading carried into the English; the same English stands over the article-less parallel at oshb:Jer.51.16 = web:Jer.51.16. Retain the note as a single-witness disclosure of the two forms with no reading preferred. TESTS the cure must pass: every recurrence sentence names its tier and the extent it claims, and survives a byte comparison of all five verse pairs -- the comparison that killed the original; and no ketiv/qere, parashah or other witness-internal claim anywhere in the row is argued from an English rendering.

rulings.challenge_claim: The unqualified statement that nothing before this verse addresses Yahweh in the second person is refuted by the bytes seventeen verses earlier in the same chapter, and the exclusivity is asserted without a swept object or a sweep count.
rulings.grounds: The clause is false as written. oshb:Jer.10.6 reads כָּמ֖וֹךָ יְהוָ֑ה גָּד֥וֹל אַתָּ֛ה וְגָד֥וֹל שִׁמְךָ֖ and oshb:Jer.10.7 opens מִ֣י לֹ֤א יִֽרָאֲךָ֙ (byte tier, both): a second-person masculine independent pronoun, second-person suffixes on the name-noun and the preposition, and a second-person verbal object, and both witnesses render them as address rather than description -- “There is no one like you, Yahweh. You are great, and your name is great in might.” (web:Jer.10.6). Those verses stand seventeen verses before the row's onset, inside the row's own chapter and inside the same parent frame, so the stated front-seam discriminator does not survive its own chapter. The claim is separately defective as an exclusivity: a first/nothing-before assertion carries an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and the unit, and is never softened by a tier label; neither is present. The boundary is not in question and the item does not ask for one: a seg follows oshb:Jer.10.22 -- at the front seam under the follow-the-verse keying (parashah tier-3, single-witness) -- and the turn into first-person petition addressed to Yahweh at oshb:Jer.10.23, יָדַ֣עְתִּי יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier), carried on by the second-person imperatives of oshb:Jer.10.24-Jer.10.25, is a speaker-role and addressee change in its own right. The defect lies in the warrant, not in the edge.
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: delete the first-occurrence clause and rest the front-seam warrant on the change it can actually carry -- the turn out of third-person report of the northern rumour at oshb:Jer.10.22 into first-person petition addressed to Yahweh from oshb:Jer.10.23, with the splice and tier already in the field. (2) If any first / only / nothing-before claim is retained anywhere in the row, attach an adjacent sweep digit naming the swept object (second-person address to Yahweh) and the unit (verses), and state its scope explicitly. TESTS the cure must pass: the replacement warrant must survive a read of oshb:Jer.10.6-Jer.10.7 -- the read that killed the original -- and no universal or exclusivity claim may stand in any field without an in-sentence digit naming its object and unit.

rulings.challenge_claim: The opening header is byte-perfect, but two byte-true catchwords cross this unit's closing seam undisclosed, the recurrence claim to the earlier header site carries no tier where one is owed, and confidence is set at high with the frontier flag unset.
rulings.grounds: Both straddles verify. שִׁמְע֕וּ אֶת דִּבְרֵ֖י הַבְּרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֑את stands at oshb:Jer.11.2 inside the span and recurs beyond the cut at oshb:Jer.11.6 as שִׁמְע֗וּ אֶת דִּבְרֵי֙ הַבְּרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את -- skeleton-identical, not byte-identical -- and those are the only two verses in the book carrying the run (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier). The summons שִׁמְע֤וּ בְקוֹלִי֙ at oshb:Jer.11.4 recurs beyond the cut at oshb:Jer.11.7 as שִׁמְע֖וּ בְּקוֹלִֽי, again skeleton-identical only (sweep: 4 verses, skeleton tier). Neither is disclosed in any field of the row, and a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the cut until it is. The counter-reading that this is ordinary sermon vocabulary rather than a device fails on the digit: a clause attested in exactly two verses book-wide is not ordinary vocabulary, and the disclosure duty does not depend on whether the device defeats the cut. The cut itself survives and should be said to survive: the fresh narrative reintroduction at oshb:Jer.11.6, וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י (byte tier; sweep: 13 verses, skeleton tier), reopens address after the prophet's own reply closes the exchange at oshb:Jer.11.5, and a seg follows oshb:Jer.11.5 at that seam (parashah tier-3, single-witness). The recurrence claim to the earlier header is untiered exactly where the strongest tier is available: הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ opens oshb:Jer.11.1, and oshb:Jer.11.1 and oshb:Jer.7.1 are identical across the whole verse (byte tier), the header core standing in exactly 11 verses (sweep: 11 verses, skeleton tier). One qualification: the confidence setting is not an independent defect. confidence and frontier_flag_considered are dependent on the disclosure repair and are re-set after it, not found against on their own; the hard whole-chapter cap arm binds chapter-length spans, and this five-verse span is not one.
rulings.remedy: (1) device_notes (or boundary_rationale): disclose both straddling runs by verse and tier -- the covenant-words summons at oshb:Jer.11.2 recurring at oshb:Jer.11.6 (skeleton tier; sweep: 2 verses) and the obey-my-voice summons at oshb:Jer.11.4 recurring at oshb:Jer.11.7 (skeleton tier; sweep: 4 verses) -- and state why they do not carry the unit across the seam: the reintroduction at oshb:Jer.11.6 reopens address after the reply at oshb:Jer.11.5. (2) boundary_rationale: tier-label the header recurrence as byte-identical to oshb:Jer.7.1 across the whole verse, with the family digit attached (sweep: 11 verses). (3) confidence and frontier_flag_considered: re-assess as dependent fields once (1) and (2) land. No boundary change is ordered. TESTS the cure must pass: the repaired row names every byte-true run that straddles either of its own seams, with the tier at which each matches; every recurrence sentence carries a tier and a digit; and the closing warrant must still stand with the straddling pair on the page -- the test the original never faced.
